subject: Re: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU capacity — final recommendations & next tests
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@acmehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-06-02T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler options

Thanks for taking the time today, Samira — helpful discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- Acme goals: predictable low-p90 latency for customer-facing completions, committed capacity for peak traffic windows, and tighter cost predictability than current spot/onsale strategies.
- Hyperscaler option (CloudX managed VMs): pros are deep ecosystem and integrated billing; cons are limited visibility into KV cache, degraded cold-start latency for short-lived containers, and spot pricing volatility for reserved-like setups.
- Redwood Dedicated: pros are reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput/SLOs, per-route throttles, automated KV/prefix caching, and transparent per-token economics. We discussed deployment options (VPC + private control plane) for regulated workloads.

Proposed next tests:
1) 48-hour steady-state throughput test against a matched CloudX reserved VM config (we'll provide a test driver and sample prompts)
2) Cold-start spike test (burst 10x RPS for 10 minutes) to validate latency SLOs
3) Cost-per-100k tokens comparison using your sample workload

Can we lock in availability for the 48-hour run next week? I'll loop in Marissa to scope the telemetry we'll collect.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler options — telemetry & next steps

Samira — good questions. Short answers up front, details below. Looping Marissa (solutions) to lead test setup.

- Isolation: Redwood Dedicated provides tenant-isolated GPU pools with scheduling that prevents noisy-neighbor VM-level interference; we run per-tenant node pinning and CPU/GPU reservations. For additional guarantees we can provision reserved nodes locked to your org during the test window.
- Cold-starts: We support warm pools and KV cache warmup hooks. For the 10-minute burst test we'll pre-warm the pool and stage KV prefixes so first-token latency is representative of production.
- Pricing: Reserved capacity is quoted as monthly committed capacity (GPU-hours + control plane fee). Pay-as-you-go is per-token + on-demand GPU time. For Q3 committed minimums we can propose a 12-month rate card with step-down pricing at higher commit tiers.

Attachments:
- capacity_comparison.csv — quick numbers matching a 4xA100 CloudX reserved VM equivalent against a 2-node Redwood Dedicated pool (see columns: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost/100k tokens)
- redwood_dedicated_sla.pdf — our standard Dedicated SLA and availability/latency targets

Telemetry we will provide for each test (sample output attached):
- Per-request latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99)
- Per-route and per-model token counts
- KV cache hit/miss rates and prefix-level metrics
- GPU utilization traces and per-node throughput
- Request traces with timestamps and model variants tried

Next steps:
1) Marissa to set up test infra and share a Telemetry spec + temporary creds (Marissa, can you add the TestPlan doc link?)
2) Samira to confirm the 48-hour window; preferred dates: Jun 15–17 or Jun 22–24
3) We'll provide a short pricing term sheet for a 12-month reserved capacity by EOD Monday (Jun 8)

Marissa, taking this offline to schedule the infra and prereqs.

Thanks,
Markus
